title: I Let the Hotel Breakfast Wristband Catch the Manager's Friends

parts.text: I paid for breakfast because my rate did not include it. They gave me a paper wristband. At the buffet a man waved four people in with no bands, laughing with the manager. I was forty, holding a plate of eggs that had cost twenty-two dollars. The sign said wristbands required. I asked the hostess. She mouthed friends. I ate. I photographed the sign, my band, their empty wrists. Then the manager told the hostess to stop seating paying guests near the window so the friends could have the view.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Paying wristbands are being moved off the window for unbanded friends.

social.video_title: The view was reserved for empty wrists — Part 1/2
social.description: Twenty-two dollar eggs, paper band, four laughers. Then the window. Would you have said something with your mouth full?

parts.text: I asked corporate, still on site, to interpret the sign. They interpreted it. The friends were offered the chance to pay or leave. Two paid. Two left. I kept the window because I had a band. The eggs were still eggs. The manager learned that friends are a rate code. My wristband went in the trash on the way to the elevator, having done a job bigger than breakfast.

social.video_title: Two paid, two left, the window came back — Part 2/2
social.description: Sign enforced, eggs digested, rate codes for everyone. Was a laugh a reservation?
